skill.description: Search AMap places, plan routes, assemble travel recommendations, and create map or heatmap links with Node.js utilities and guided workflows.
skill.summary: Use AMap services for place discovery, route planning, travel research, and geographic visualization.
skill.author: AMap-Web

security_audit.summary: Most high and medium static alerts are false positives caused by JavaScript templates, Markdown backticks, Chinese text entropy, or fixed configuration paths. Confirmed risks include outbound AMap requests, plaintext key persistence, credential exposure, mandatory telemetry, and insecure HTTP heatmap links. No prompt injection or obfuscated executable payload was found.

remediation.issue: User-controlled values are placed in shell commands.
remediation.suggestion: Use the Node.js HTTP client and URL APIs instead of constructed curl commands. Validate and encode every parameter before requests.

remediation.issue: The workflow asks users to reveal an API key and places it on command lines.
remediation.suggestion: Require environment-based key configuration. Never request keys in chat, and redact credentials from errors, logs, examples, and generated links.

remediation.issue: Usage telemetry runs before workflows without consent.
remediation.suggestion: Remove mandatory logging or make it opt-in. Explain the destination, fields, purpose, and retention before requesting consent.

remediation.issue: The API key can be stored in plaintext config.json.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer environment or secret-store access. If local storage remains, create the file with owner-only permissions and document rotation.
Use an HTTPS heatmap endpoint and require HTTPS data sources. Reject credentials or private tokens embedded in data URLs.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Usage Telemetry Without Consent
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs agents to call the AMap logging endpoint before six workflows. These mandatory requests reveal skill usage and workflow labels without user consent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Each cited workflow explicitly says to send an analytics request before performing the requested operation.

semantic_findings.title: User Input Interpolated Into a Shell Command
semantic_findings.description: The documented curl command inserts a user-supplied location and API key into a double-quoted shell string. Shell substitutions can execute if input is not safely encoded.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions define placeholders from user input and place them directly inside a bash curl command without shell-safe argument construction.

semantic_findings.title: API Key Requested in Chat and Exposed on Command Line

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited instructions explicitly request the key from the user and include the key placeholder in the command URL.

content.user_title: Plan Routes and Find Places with AMap
content.value_statement: Map research often requires separate place, route, and visualization workflows. This skill connects AMap searches, routing APIs, travel planning, and map-link generation.
actual_capabilities: Searches AMap places by keyword, city, type, coordinates, radius, and pagination parameters.
Requests walking, driving, cycling, and public transit routes between coordinates.
Builds travel recommendations by searching several interest categories in one city.
Generates AMap visualization links from place and route task data.
Creates direct AMap search, nearby search, and heatmap links through documented workflows.
Loads an AMap key from environment variables or a local configuration file.
limitations: Live searches and routes require a valid AMap Web Service key and network access.
Search terms, coordinates, API keys, and documented usage events can be sent to AMap.
Documented command-line scripts are absent; the included module mainly exposes JavaScript functions.
The travel planner returns place results only, despite documentation describing route and map-link outputs.

use_cases.title: Research a City Visit
use_cases.description: Find attractions, food, and hotels, then organize the results for a city itinerary.

use_cases.title: Add Location Features
use_cases.description: Call AMap place and routing services from a Node.js application using the exported functions.

use_cases.title: Visualize Geographic Data
use_cases.description: Create map or heatmap links for coordinate-based datasets hosted at an accessible URL.

prompt_templates.prompt: Using my configured AMap key, find [category] near [location] within [radius] meters. Summarize the leading results with addresses.
prompt_templates.scenario: Nearby search with a configured credential

prompt_templates.prompt: Plan walking, driving, cycling, and transit routes from [origin coordinates] to [destination coordinates]. Compare distance, duration, and major steps.

Addresses and coordinates when returned by AMap.

output_examples.input: Compare walking and driving from point A to point B.
output_examples.output: A concise comparison of distance, estimated duration, and route differences for both modes.

best_practices: Store the AMap key in an environment variable and avoid sharing it in chat.
Confirm the city and coordinate order before requesting routes or nearby searches.
Tell users which data and usage events will be sent to AMap before making requests.
anti_patterns: Do not place real API keys in prompts, command lines, generated links, or committed files.
Do not execute shell commands built from unescaped place names or other user input.
Do not use plaintext HTTP links for private or sensitive geographic datasets.

faq.question: Do I need an AMap API key?
faq.answer: Direct search links do not require a key. Live place searches, geocoding, and route requests require a valid key.

faq.question: Where can the skill read the key?
faq.answer: It reads AMAP_KEY or AMAP_WEBSERVICE_KEY. It can also read a plaintext config.json file.

faq.question: What information is sent to AMap?
faq.answer: Requests can include search terms, locations, coordinates, route endpoints, the API key, and fixed usage-event labels.

faq.question: Can I use the documented command-line scripts?
faq.answer: No. The referenced scripts directory is not included, so use the exported functions in index.js.

faq.question: Which route modes are supported?
faq.answer: The module supports walking, driving, cycling, and public transit route requests.

faq.question: Can it generate heatmaps?
faq.answer: The instructions generate an AMap heatmap link from a hosted data URL. They do not render or validate the dataset locally.
